current_unit: Task 6: Cadence policy and a review rule (docs/plans/2026-09-28-dependency-currency.md, Layer 4)
notes: Task 5 (Layer 3, staleness alarm) landed 2026-09-28: scripts/check-electron-support.js and .github/workflows/dependency-currency.yml committed. Bumped actions/checkout and actions/setup-node in the new workflow from the plan's literal v4 pin to v7, matching ci.yml/build-release.yml's already-current convention in this repo. releases.electronjs.org is network-blocked in this sandbox (same class of restriction as docs.github.com noted for Task 4) and gh CLI is not installed here, so Steps 2-3's local verification used a mocked fetch (representative release-index data) instead of the live endpoint, and the gh call failed with ENOENT rather than an auth error -- both are consistent with what those steps are actually checking (the support-window computation and printed issue body), not the network/gh path itself. Confirmed it alarms on a forced electron 32.3.3 (computes majors-behind correctly) and stays quiet on a forced 44.4.5 ("OK: ... inside the supported line", no gh call attempted). Lockfile restored cleanly after both trials (git diff --exit-code passed). Step 6 (gh workflow run to trigger it for real against the live 573-days-stale Electron 32 and open the proof issue) could not be done from this session -- no gh access, and workflow_dispatch needs the workflow merged to the default branch first. That live trigger-and-verify is a deferred follow-up for a human or a later firing with real GitHub access; until it happens, Layer 3's alarm exists in code but has not yet produced its real, on-record proof issue. vitest (81 files / 1226 tests) and tsc --noEmit both clean after `npm ci` + `npm run install:companion`. Next unit is Task 6 (Layer 4): Step 1 picks the upgrade cadence (every-major vs every-other-major vs every-third-major) against the show calendar -- that is an explicit human decision per the plan's own text ("the cadence number is a human decision"), not something to guess at. The next firing should not silently pick one; it should either find a cadence already chosen (e.g. left in a repo file or a prior note) or set status to blocked with a clear note asking for the pick, per orchestrator step 10, before touching Steps 2-3 (the CLAUDE.md review-rule edit, which is plan-doable on its own but references the chosen cadence in spirit even though the literal CLAUDE.md text given in the plan doesn't hardcode a number).
